decision: Allowed values are any integer in [0,255], not restricted to input values
rationale: The problem says 'at most k integers from this range [0..255]'. Sample 3 confirms this: with values {0,25,50,255} and k=2, the optimal representatives are not from the input set (e.g., ~12 or 13 and 255), yielding SSE=37500000.
When values are sorted and each pixel maps to its nearest representative, optimal clusters are always contiguous intervals. This allows a standard interval DP approach.

decision: For each contiguous group, check floor and ceil of weighted mean as candidate representative
rationale: The optimal real-valued representative is the weighted mean. Since we need an integer, the best integer representative is either floor or ceil of the mean. We compute both and pick the one with lower cost.

The problem is a self-contained competitive programming problem solvable with ~100-200 lines of Python. All logic (parsing, precomputation, DP, output) shares the same data and is naturally implemented together.
